we demonstrated that the scattering spectrum of a plasmonically coupled nanoparticle pair can be used for the localization imaging of a nanoparticle pair.
the scattering spectrum of a nanoparticle pair is strongly influenced by the plasmon coupling effect.
wavelength-resolved dark field microscopy can be used to localize plasmonic nanoparticles with sub-diffraction-limit accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the localization imaging of a single plasmonic particle with wavelength-resolved microscopy.

the wavelength-resolved scattering spectrum of a single plasmonic nanostructure, which can provide the information about the center-of-mas localization of the plasmonic nanopair, and the scattering intensity ratio of the individual nanoparticles.
the development of a wavelength-resolved darkfield microscopy technique for the sub-diffraction-limit imaging of a plasmonic nanoparticle pair.

the wavelength-resolved scattering spectra of the plasmonic nanoparticles with different gap distances can be used to obtain accurate information about the center of mass localization.

the optical localization information determined from a single plasmonic particle pair could be well defined and consistent with the SEM measurements when the gap distance of the pair was larger than 20 nm.
the optical localization imaging of a pair of plasmonic nanoparticles with wavelength-resolved optical microscopy is feasible when the inter-particle distance is larger than 20 nm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, when the gap distance between two nanoparticles was less than 30 nm, the scattering spectra of nanoparticle pairs were seriously modulated by plasmonic coupling.
the optical method could be used to determine the center-of-mas localization information of a single plasmonic nanorod pair with a gap distance of more than 20 nm.

the wavelength-resolved dark field microscopy could provide the center-of-masses localization information of the nanoparticle pairs when the gap distance between the nanoparticles was larger than 20 nm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to consider the gap distance and orientation of the plasmonic nanoparitcle pairs in the optical imaging studies.

the optical measurement of the localization of a plasmonically coupled nanoparticle pair can be performed only when the gap distance between the two particles is larger than the wavelength of the incident light.
the plasmonic interaction effect between the two nanoparticles should be taken into account for the optical localization measurements of plasmonic nanoparicle pairs.
